producer_report.summary:
Root cause: `carry` and `prior_result_section` dropped the files the earlier job's candidate changed, the producer's own account and the measured check results. `check_prior_result_and_scope` only tested that the job id was named, so a retry could name the job and still keep or drop its work without saying so. The fix is in all three places.

- **`carry`**: `EarlierAttempt` gains `changed_files`, `changed_files_omitted`, `approach` and `checks`. `carry` fills them from the `Candidate` and `Verification` records, so no record, schema or allow-list entry is added.
  - Files are `status path`, at most 30. The rest, and any path that redaction altered, are counted as omitted.
  - The approach is the producer's report summary, redacted and cut to about 800 characters.
  - Checks are one line each (`name: passed|failed (exit code N, M tests ran)`), at most 20, with no output text.
- **Brief**: the section prints these for the retried and the referenced jobs, with 'none recorded for it' lines when empty. The intro and READING_RULES rule 1 mention the files; no prompt file changed.
- **Check**: the new part, "the earlier job's files", refuses a reading unless each carried file is a deliverable (or under a directory deliverable) or is named in an out_of_scope item, as its own path or an ancestor directory. Matching is by whole path token, and survey prose, summary and criteria never count. A file whose name redaction altered is never demanded.
- **Fake reader and tests**: the fake reader names the earlier job's files in its out_of_scope item. New unit tests cover `carry`, the brief, the check (abandoned and rejected shapes, a table of which priors are refused, boundary cases, redaction) and the declared share. Integration tests cover retry.rs, lifecycle.rs and a new run/mod.rs test. Five existing retry.rs tests had a retry reader that ignored a file the first attempt added, so they now exclude greeting.txt in out_of_scope.
- **CHANGELOG.md**: records the root cause and the fix. It also says job 20261027-054209-z7sj was dispatched, never verified and had no findings, so this retry starts from the base. It declares 'refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings', as a declared expectation rather than a measurement."

120 passed, including the new carry, check_prior_result, path-token and declared-intended tests
5 passed, including the new fake-reader files test
16 passed; 5 existing tests needed their retry reader to say what becomes of greeting.txt
first run failed on my own wrong assertion (the check line has '0 tests ran'); fixed the assertion, then reran. The final rerun's output was not read; lifecycle also ran in the full workspace run

Job 20261027-054209-z7sj was dispatched and never verified, with no findings; this retry starts from the base.

Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`; the test fails on the base commit and passes with the change.

It asserts exactly 30 'status path' files, the redacted path dropped, omitted == 6, the approach start kept, bounded to 800 chars and token-free, and the check lines with pass/fail, exit code and test count and no output text. Two more tests cover no candidate and the 20-line check cap. `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading` gave 120 passed. On the base the new EarlierAttempt fields do not exist, so the test cannot compile.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs shows `reader_brief` prints the files touched and the approach for both a retried job and a referenced job, and prints a 'none recorded' line when no candidate exists. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-context briefs`.
criteria_check.evidence: Tests a_retry_brief_prints_files_approach_and_checks_of_the_earlier_job, a_referenced_job_brief_prints_files_approach_and_checks and a_prior_without_a_candidate_says_none_recorded pass in `cargo test --locked -p athena-context briefs` (66 passed). The last one asserts the three 'none recorded for it' lines appear once for the retried slot and once for the referenced slot.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test shows `check_prior_result_and_scope` refuses a reading that names the job id but neither lists nor excludes a prior job's changed files, and accepts one that does. It uses prior jobs of at least two failure shapes (dispatched/abandoned unverified, rejected with findings), not one job id. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core check_prior_result`.
criteria_check.evidence: check_prior_result_refuses_files_the_reading_neither_lists_nor_excludes_for_both_failure_shapes builds an abandoned job (no verification, no outcome) and a rejected job (failed check, outcome rejected) through the real `carry`. Each is refused with "the earlier job's files" and the file names, with neither 'the previous result' nor 'the change scope', and each is accepted when the files are deliverables, under a directory deliverable, or named in out_of_scope as a path or an ancestor directory. Regression tests cover survey prose, sibling paths, token boundaries, redaction-dropped paths and multiple priors. All pass in the reading run.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more readings (retries whose prior job changed files but whose reading ignores them); the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings, because only retries with a recorded candidate are affected.
criteria_check.evidence: The table test check_prior_result_refuses_only_priors_with_recorded_files_the_reading_ignores refuses exactly the two 'ignores' rows (abandoned and rejected shapes) and accepts no-candidate, no-changes, listed and excluded rows. prior_result_refusal_is_declared_intended asserts replay_declaration gives share Some(5) for 'expected 5% of newly refused readings', that the doc comment of check_prior_result_and_scope has 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and says the replay passes no earlier attempts, and that the CHANGELOG has the same phrases. The 5% is a declared expectation, not a measurement: the replay gives the checks no earlier attempts, so it cannot observe this check.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the producer summary is redacted first and then shortened, not shortened and then redacted. This way a cut can never leave half a secret in the brief.

The retry reader in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs (`second_attempt`) now excludes greeting.txt in out_of_scope. Other retrying test readers (scope_guard.rs, status.rs, evidence_labels.rs, run_pin_tests.rs) needed no change in the full run, as far as the tool's lack of a failure exit shows.
The 5% is a declared expectation, not a measurement, because the replay cannot see this check. The CHANGELOG and doc comment say so.

The check accepts a bare ancestor such as `crates/` written as its own token in an out_of_scope item. That is a deliberate explicit exclusion; the same words in a survey, summary or criterion do not count.
mistakes: My first fake.rs parser assumed quoted '> ' lines, but `section()` strips them, so my own new fake test failed once. I fixed the parser.
My first lifecycle assertion expected 'test: failed (exit code 1)', but the check ran 0 tests, so the line is 'exit code 1, 0 tests ran'. I fixed the assertion.
I could not read the full-suite output (it was saved outside the working directory), so I know the suite passed only from the missing failure exit.
learnings: `section()` in fake.rs strips the leading '> ' from quoted lines, so the fake reader sees `status path` lines, not quoted ones. Its parser keys on the 'Files its candidate changed (' header and stops at the first line that does not start with a status word.

Existing retry tests with a scripted first attempt that edits more than README.md (retry.rs `first_attempt` adds greeting.txt) now need the retry reader to list or exclude that file. That is the intended effect of the new check.
`check_reading_text` and the replay give the checks no earlier attempts, so a replay cannot observe the new part of `check_prior_result_and_scope`.
JobRecords with no outcome and no verification can be built directly in reading.rs tests (`job_with_checks` with `verification = None`) to model an abandoned job.
desires: A way to read a saved tool-output file (it sat outside the working directory), or a quiet mode so the full-suite result fits on screen.
The brief says the reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom, but the brief the tests print shows 'reader: 1906 of 2000 tokens used, 94 left'. The figure in the task text looks stale.
